scenarios.title: Repair demand-mounted reports and audit data
scenarios.summary: Connect directory keys to their intended virtual filesystems and distinguish saved maps from existing mounts.
scenarios.objective: Repair the indirect map under /srv/teams using single-directory keys in /etc/auto.teams and the supplied 30-second idle timeout. Connect /srv/teams/reports to original /dev/ledger/reports with read/write access, and /srv/teams/audit to original /dev/ledger/audit with read-only access. After saving all edits and applying any required refresh or idle check, read keep.txt at both paths. Current mounts and a new lookup after expiry must select the intended original data. Keep the supplied storage and file data unchanged. Save every edited file, then choose Check work.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the failed saved-policy, active-policy, current-mount and new-lookup checks separately. A correct saved file does not refresh a direct map or replace a current backing mount.

/keep.txt.contents: ledger/reports: daily service reports, original dataset.
ledger/audit: protected audit history, original dataset.
demo-indirect/reports: daily service reports, original dataset.
demo-indirect/audit: protected audit history, original dataset.

reference.explanation: An indirect key is the single directory name below the master directory. Correct the two sources and retain the access options. Fill this example, then Save file.
The old backing mount still returns the audit dataset even after saving a correct indirect map. Saving does not replace an existing mount.
Choose Run idle check (30 s). This advances only the simulator clock and expires the supplied nonbusy old backing mount. No Linux command or real waiting is involved.
This new lookup should return the original reports dataset. cat both triggers the mount and reads the actual simulated file.
Verify the second path independently: it should return the audit dataset with read-only backing access.
Compare actual current backing sources and rw/ro options. This supported filter lists only the provided ext4 mounts, not the separate autofs trigger filesystem.

steps: Inspect the supplied maps and actual backing data
Repair and save the required configuration
Apply the needed refresh or idle check and verify both data paths
Check work and repair remaining mismatches
hints: Compare the managed directory in the master with the path you are trying to read. Is its key one directory name or a full path?
Keep the leading dash on fstype=ext4 options and the colon before each local /dev source. ro and rw describe backing filesystem access.
Indirect edits are consulted on a new lookup. Master/direct changes need systemctl reload autofs here. Existing mounts keep their association until the simulator idle check expires them.
scenarios.explanation: An indirect master directory combines with each single-component key. Correcting a saved indirect map affects the next new lookup without a reload, but an already mounted filesystem retains its old association until expiry. Verify both the present data and the future policy.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded local ext4 FILE maps over supplied in-memory storage only. The already-running automounter and explicit nonbusy idle checks are simulated; no host shell, daemon, mounts, files, clock or network. Only supplied cat paths, findmnt -t ext4 [provided point], and systemctl reload autofs are supported. One backing mount per filesystem, no busy handles, at most two master rows and four trigger points. Changing root/timeout/direct-key structure while mounted requires expiry first in this simulator; that is not a universal Linux rule. NFS/program/NSS maps, includes, substitution, wildcards and other options are unsupported. Sources checked2026-11-07; no full objective coverage claimed.

scenarios.title: Convert indirect directories to direct AutoFS paths
scenarios.summary: Move a local map to direct full-path triggers and verify that saved edits reach active lookup policy.
scenarios.objective: Convert the supplied configuration to a direct map: /- in the master, full mountpoint paths in /etc/auto.direct, and a 30-second idle timeout. Connect /srv/direct/reports to original /dev/handover/reports with read/write access, and /srv/direct/audit to original /dev/handover/audit with read-only access. After saving all edits and applying any required refresh or idle check, read keep.txt at both paths. Current mounts and a new lookup after expiry must select the intended original data. Keep the supplied storage and file data unchanged. Save every edited file, then choose Check work.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the failed saved-policy, active-policy, current-mount and new-lookup checks separately. A correct saved file does not refresh a direct map or replace a current backing mount.
